get_api.description: Look one API up by its provider, and the service name when it has one, and get back everything the directory knows about it: the title, the full description, the categories, the logo, when it was added and last updated, every version it holds and the one it recommends, and the addresses of its OpenAPI definition in JSON and YAML - ready to fetch with an HTTP step or hand to a code generator. Name a version to describe that one instead of the recommended one. No account or API key required.
get_api.display_str_template: Look up an API from provider '{0}'.

get_api.name: get_api

parameters.description: The provider's name as the directory lists it - usually its domain, e.g. 'googleapis.com', 'github.com' or 'apis.guru'. Chain it from 'List providers'.
parameters.name: provider

parameters.description: Optional. The service name, for a provider that publishes several APIs, e.g. 'drive' under 'googleapis.com'. Chain it from 'List a provider's services' or from an API's 'service' field. Leave blank for a provider with a single API.
parameters.name: service

parameters.description: Optional. The version to describe, e.g. 'v3' or '2.2.0', exactly as the API's 'versions' list names it. Leave blank for the version the directory recommends.
parameters.name: version

added.description: When the API was first added to the directory, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

categories.description: The categories the directory files the API under, e.g. 'financial' or 'developer_tools'. Any of them can be searched for.

description.description: The API's full description, as its definition gives it - often several paragraphs of Markdown.

docs_url.description: The API's own documentation, when the definition names it. Null otherwise.

entry_url.description: The address of this version's own entry in the directory.

id.description: The API's id in the directory: the provider, then a colon and the service name when there is one, e.g. 'googleapis.com:drive' or 'apis.guru'.

is_preferred.description: True when the version described is the one the directory recommends. False in a provider listing means a newer or older version is held than the recommended one - look the API up for it.

logo_url.description: The address of the API's logo, when there is one. Null otherwise.

openapi_version.description: The OpenAPI (or Swagger) version the definition is written in, e.g. '3.0.0' or '2.0'.

origin_url.description: Where the directory fetched the definition from - usually the provider's own published copy. Null when not recorded.

provider.description: The provider that publishes the API - its domain, e.g. 'googleapis.com'. What 'List a provider's APIs' and 'Get an API' take.

service.description: The service name, for a provider that publishes several APIs, e.g. 'drive'. Null for a provider with a single API.

spec_json_url.description: The address of the definition as JSON. Fetch it with an HTTP step to read the API's paths and schemas.

spec_yaml_url.description: The address of the same definition as YAML.

summary.description: The first paragraph of the API's description, on one line and cut to about 200 characters. 'Get an API' carries the whole text.

title.description: The API's title, as its definition gives it.

unofficial.description: True when the definition was written by the community rather than published by the provider.

updated.description: When this version's definition was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

version.description: The version this record describes, e.g. 'v3' or '2.2.0'. A provider listing holds one version of each API, usually its newest.

version_added.description: When this version was added to the directory, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

version_count.description: How many versions the directory holds.

versions.description: Every version of the API the directory holds. Any of them can be named in 'Get an API'.

get_metrics.description: Read the directory's own numbers: how many APIs, providers, definitions and endpoints it holds, how many APIs were added and updated in the last week, and how many definitions are unofficial, unreachable or invalid. list_provider_apis.description: List the APIs one provider publishes, each with its title, a one-line summary, its categories and the address of its OpenAPI definition. The provider's index holds one version of each API - usually its newest - and says whether it is the one the directory recommends; look an API up for its recommended version and every version it holds. Filter by text, and page with a limit: a provider like Google publishes hundreds. No account or API key required.

search_apis.description: Search every API in the directory by a word in its name, title, provider or description, by the category it is filed under, or both, and get back a page of results in order of title, or with the most recently added or updated first. Each result carries the API's title, summary, categories, every version it holds and the one the directory recommends, and the address of its OpenAPI definition. The way to find out whether an API has a published definition, or to watch what the directory adds. No account or API key required.

description: The Wikipedia for Web APIs: a free, open directory of machine-readable API definitions in OpenAPI format, covering thousands of APIs from hundreds of providers - Google, Microsoft, Amazon, GitHub, Twilio and many more. Search it by keyword or category, list a provider's APIs and services, look one API up by name and version to get its title, description, categories, logo and the address of its OpenAPI definition in JSON or YAML, or read the directory's own metrics. For workflows that discover APIs, catalogue them or feed their definitions into other tools. API definitions supplied by APIs.guru (https://apis.guru). No account or API key required.
